data.body:
DESIGN DECISIONS (settled with maintainer @JoeOakhartNava, to be implemented). Landing order: this ticket FIRST, then bb9b.

Change 1 — cadence: rebar-autodeploy.timer 2min -> HOURLY. Document the staleness tradeoff AND the on-demand escape hatch (`systemctl start rebar-autodeploy.service`) in BOTH the unit file and the runbook.

Change 2 — the vote/no-vote split:
* Retryable -> NO VOTE (leave the change vote-less so the backfill reconciler re-drives it): review-error, llm-unavailable, scanner, and process-teardown-mid-review.
* Terminal -> VOTE -1:
  - finding (unchanged);
  - gate-disabled — a configuration state that yields the IDENTICAL result forever, so a no-vote would make backfill retry it forever (the invisible-infinite-loop this ticket warns against). It votes -1;
  - indeterminate — a genuine concluded "could not determine" is a real fail-closed veto, so it votes -1 (terminal).
  Both gate-disabled and indeterminate remain manually re-triggerable via bb9b (indeterminate is eligible there; gate-disabled is refused).

Teardown-vs-conclusion boundary (the critical discriminator): app.py shutdown/drain sets a shutdown/cancel flag (cancel scope) that the voter checks; a CancelledError raised during drain is treated as retryable NO-VOTE rather than falling through to the fail-closed -1 conversion. A verdict that actually reached an indeterminate conclusion still votes.

Bounded-retry escalation (AC6): after N vote-less attempts on the SAME revision, escalate by BOTH casting the -1 (so a human / bb9b sees it) AND emitting the CloudWatch metric.

Constraints preserved: (1) vote-less must remain unsubmittable — verify no degraded mode (RECONCILE_DEGRADED) turns "no vote" into submittable; (2) genuinely vote-less — nothing provisional posted on the change, or backfill re-suppresses.
